transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-01
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (AtlasPay VP Eng), Maya Ortiz (AtlasPay SRE), Liam Chen (AtlasPay Product)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick agenda — canary plan, cutover steps, monitoring and runbooks. I think we have 45 minutes, so we'll try to be tight.
[00:18] Jordan: Sounds good, Alex. Quick context — engineering and SRE want low-risk cutover, we want to limit initial blast radius to a small customer cohort.
[00:30] Priya: Great, so our recommendation from the SE side is a staged canary: 5% traffic for 48h, check error / latency and quality metrics, then 25% for 24-48h, then 100% if green. We also propose automatic rollback thresholds on p95 and error rate.
[00:52] Maya: When you say p95 thresholds, what numbers are we thinking? Our current baseline is 120ms p95 on embedding calls, but generation is more variable.
[01:10] Priya: Right, for Redwood Hosted we saw p95 ~180-220ms on similar workloads; for Dedicated it drops to ~90-130ms. For safety I'd suggest p95 < 350ms and error rate < 0.5% as initial canary pass. Those are configurable.
[01:32] Jordan: Okay, AtlasPay's SLA for payments backend is stricter, but for this feature 350ms is acceptable for canary. We also need a manual rollback path.
[01:45] Alex: On rollback, we'll provide an automated fallback to the previous model endpoint + an explicit manual cutover button in Console. Also, we can route failing requests to a lower-cost compatible variant if needed.
[02:05] Liam: For A/B testing, can we run a split where 50% goes to Redwood variant A with quantization and 50% to variant B unquantized, to measure quality delta?
[02:20] Priya: Yep that's doable. We'll need to define evaluation prompts and automatic quality checks; Redwood Optimize recommends sampling 500 requests across cohorts during the canary.
[02:35] Maya: About monitoring, what dashboards will we get out of box? We need token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency, error rates, and traces tied back to request IDs.
[02:50] Priya: Console provides per-route/model dashboards, p50/p95/p99, token cost, and tracing hooks. We can push metrics to your Prometheus or create Datadog integration. For alerts, we recommend: p95 > threshold, error rate > threshold, and quality regression alert based on eval set.
[03:12] Jordan: Do you support SSO and audit logs for the control plane during cutover? Security wants to see activity & KMS usage.
[03:24] Alex: Yes, SSO via SAML/Okta is supported, plus detailed audit logs and KMS integration for key management. We'll attach our SOC2 docs in the follow-up.
[03:36] Maya: On private deployments, we need VPC peering and specific IP ranges. Who is the contact at Redwood to exchange network details?
[03:48] Alex: That'll be me; Jordan, please send the VPC and peering contact, and we'll loop in infra. Action item: we'll share the networking checklist.
[04:00] Jordan: Sure.
[04:05] Priya: Going back to canary traffic routing — we need to decide whether to do header-based routing for customer cohorts or percentage-based. Header-based is safer if you have distinct customer IDs.
[04:21] Liam: We have customer IDs but some are multi-tenant; I'd prefer percentage-based tied to a set of beta customers. We can provide a list.
[04:33] Priya: Perfect. We'll implement a canary that matches an allowlist for the first 5% wave, then ramp % after. Also recommend sticky sessions for session-based behavior.
[04:50] Maya: Runbooks — can you walk through what the rollback steps look like? I want to ensure our on-call knows exactly what to do.
[05:02] Priya: Sure. Quick outline: 1) Detect anomaly via alert -> 2) Triager runs checkpoint diagnostics (latency histograms, top error traces) -> 3) Flip traffic to previous model or to fallback variant via Console -> 4) Postmortem and quality analysis. We'll provide a runnable playbook with CLI commands and Console screenshots.
[05:30] Jordan: How fast is flip? Can we do sub-30s cutover?
[05:36] Priya: In most cases yes, traffic re-routing is near-instant; propagation depends on your edge and caching. For K-V cache concerns, we have prefix invalidation and options to warm caches.
[05:52] Maya: Cache warming — if we cutover to new model, do we need to rebuild KV cache? That could increase latency initially.
[06:03] Priya: There is a warm-up period if the model variant has different cache state. We recommend starting canary with a synthetic warm-up script that hits a representative prompt set to populate KV cache before opening traffic. We'll include that in the runbook.
[06:20] Liam: For the A/B quality eval, what's the easiest way to run automatic comparisons?
[06:28] Priya: Redwood Optimize can run prompt set evals and surface regression alerts. For the POC we can run nightly evals and flag if quality delta exceeds agreed threshold.
[06:40] Jordan: Pricing — if we go Dedicated, what commitments are we looking at and how long to provision?
[06:50] Alex: Dedicated has monthly reserved capacity; from commit to provisioning it's typically 2-3 weeks depending on capacity and region. We'll send you a pricing sheet with options for burst capacity.
[07:05] Jordan: Ok please send that.
[07:09] Alex: Action item noted — I'll follow up.
[07:12] Priya: One more infra nuance — for on-prem or VPC deployments, we surface audit logs and KMS support but HSM integration may require an enterprise link. We'll flag any compliance needs.
[07:28] Maya: We do need HSM for certain keys; we'll highlight that in the security questionnaire.
[07:34] Liam: For rollout schedule, what's the tentative timeline you recommend?
[07:40] Priya: If you can confirm canary cohort this week, run dry-run next week (week of 2026-07-13), production cutover target late July. So roughly 2-3 week runway.
[07:54] Jordan: That aligns with our product timeline.
[08:00] Alex: Ok let's go through a quick run-through of the cutover checklist — we'll call out pre-cutover validations, canary waves, monitoring, rollback, and post-cutover validation.
[08:12] Priya: Pre-cutover: network peering, certs, canary config in Console, warm-up script, alert thresholds set, eval prompt set loaded. Canary wave 1: 5% or allowlist for 48h. Monitor quality and SLOs. Wave 2: 25% for 24-48h. Full ramp: 100% after green.
[08:38] Maya: Who owns the decision at each gate?
[08:42] Alex: We propose triage owner is AtlasPay SRE (Maya) for immediate rollback decision, product (Liam) and Redwood SE (Priya) for quality sign-off. AE will coordinate communications.
[08:58] Jordan: Good. For observability, can we get a weekly snapshot report during canary?
[09:04] Priya: Yes, we can auto-generate a canary report with latency histograms, error breakdown and sample traces. We'll set it to daily during canary and weekly after.
[09:18] Liam: Any mention of legal/procurement — do we need additional paperwork for Dedicated?
[09:24] Alex: There's a standard enterprise addendum for Dedicated capacity and private deployment; procurement usually wants SOC2 and DPA. We'll send those docs.
[09:34] Jordan: Please include data retention specifics in the DPA.
[09:39] Alex: Will do.
[09:42] Priya: Clarifying one technical detail — if we need to fallback to a smaller quantized variant, there may be small quality differences; we'll surface those in the report. Make sure success criteria account for acceptable quality delta.
[09:58] Maya: What's the plan for rate limiting during canary?
[10:02] Priya: We recommend conservative rate limits on the canary cohort to avoid burst behavior; also enable quotas per route.
[10:10] Jordan: For the dry-run, do you want us to open a maintenance window?
[10:13] Alex: If you prefer low-risk, schedule maintenance window for the dry-run but it's not strictly required if canary is limited to a small set.
[10:20] Maya: We'll tentatively plan a dry-run during off-peak next week.
[10:25] Alex: Great. Anything else?
[10:28] Liam: One ask — can Redwood provide a sample incident runbook in markdown we can import into our on-call tooling?
[10:34] Priya: Yep, we'll include an import-ready markdown runbook and link to Console screenshots.
[10:40] Jordan: Thanks.
[10:42] Alex: Ok, we'll recap next steps now.
[10:45] Priya: Recap: Redwood to share canary runbook, warm-up script, and pricing. AtlasPay to provide canary cohort and VPC peering contact. Set dry-run week of 2026-07-13.
[10:58] Jordan: Sounds good, thanks all.
[11:01] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments.

End of transcript.
